answer: Environmental entropy anchoring mitigates Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to real-time telemetry from remote stations, such as a marine inlet, timber forest, or alpine glacier. Validators challenge agents for unpredictable microclimate readings signed by on-site hardware security modules. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of deploying distinct physical sensor nodes per identity. However, severe weather and hardware drift can cause legitimate nodes to fail verification.
